'''Clifford Victor Johnson''' (born 5 March 1968)<ref>Career data from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is a British [[theoretical physicist]] and professor at the [[UCSB]] department of [[Physics]].

==Biography==
Johnson was born in London, England,<ref name="Clifford Johnson's Biography">{{Cite web |title=Clifford Johnson's Biography |url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/clifford-johnson-41 |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=The HistoryMakers |language=en}}</ref> and lived in [[Montserrat]] for 10 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/johnson_cliffordv.html|title=Clifford V. Johnson - Mathematician of the African Diaspora|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> From an early age, Johnson was interested in electronics. He would spend time reading on the subject, and designing small machinery such as radios.<ref name="Clifford Johnson's Biography"/> He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Physics from [[Imperial College London]] in 1989 and he completed his Doctor of Philosophy in Mathematics and Physics from the [[University of Southampton]] in 1992.{{cn|date=October 2026}}

Johnson's research focus is in [[superstring theory]] and [[particle physics]], specifically related to strongly coupled phenomena.<ref>[http://www.sciencenews.org/view/feature/id/42632/title/Strings_Link_the_Ultracold_with_the_Superhot Strings Link the Ultracold With the Superhot] ''Science News'', 25 April 2009,</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Timmer |first=John |title=String Theory Officially Useful, May Not Represent Reality |date=17 February 2009 |work=[[Ars Technica]] |url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2009/02/string-theory-officially-useful-may-not-represent-reality/}}</ref> He has previously worked at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Durham University]] and [[Princeton University]] as a postdoctoral fellow.<ref name="faculty">{{Cite web|url=http://dornsifelive.usc.edu/wrapper/cf/faculty-and-staff/faculty.cfm|title=Faculty Profile > USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences|website=dornsifelive.usc.edu}}</ref> He worked as an assistant professor at the University of Kentucky from 1997 to 1999, and has been a physics professor at the University of Southern California's Department of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name="Clifford Johnson's Biography"/> In July 2023, he returned to the University of California, Santa Barbara. He received the 2005 [[Maxwell Medal and Prize]] from the Institute of Physics, "For his outstanding contribution to string theory, [[quantum gravity]] and its interface with strongly coupled field theory, in particular for his work on understanding the censorship of singularities and the thermodynamic properties of [[quantum spacetime]].<ref>[http://www.iop.org/activity/awards/Early_career_awards/The_Maxwell_Medal_and_Prize/Maxwell_medal_recipients/page_10193.html Recipients of the Maxwell Medal and Prize] Institute of Physics</ref><ref>[http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29175/2 Faces and Places] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220104546/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29175/2 |date=20 February 2012 }} ''Cern Courier'' 4 October 2004</ref><ref>[http://college.usc.edu/news/stories/38/u-k-society-lauds-usc-college-physics-professor/ U.K. Society Lauds USC College Professor] ''USC College News'' 1 October 2004</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080205050256/http://www.pbs.org/kcet/wiredscience/education/2008/01/careers-in-science-professor-o.html Careers in Science: Professor of Physics] ''Wired Science'' 11 January 2008</ref> He received a [[National Science Foundation]] [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|CAREER Award]] in 1997.<ref name=faculty /> In 2005, [[The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education]] listed Clifford Johnson as the most highly cited black professor of mathematics or a related field at an American university or college.<ref>[http://www.jbhe.com/news_views/49_mostcited_blackmathematicians.html The Most Highly Cited Black Mathematicians] ''The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education'' 2005</ref> He was named a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|access-date=2021-10-15|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2022, Johnson was award AIP's Andrew Gemant award for his artistic and creative approach towards physics outreach and education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics is Culture: Clifford V. Johnson Selected for AIP's 2022 Andrew Gemant Award {{!}} American Institute of Physics |url=https://www.aip.org/news/physics-culture-clifford-v-johnson-selected-aips-2022-andrew-gemant-award |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=www.aip.org}}</ref> Johnson has also been awarded the Institute of Physics' James Clerk Maxwell Medal and Prize.<ref name="inverse.com">{{Cite web |date=2020-09-23 |title=How to become one of the world's top physicists — and have an IMDB page |url=https://www.inverse.com/mind-body/clifford-johnson-physics-rookie-year |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=Inverse |language=en}}</ref>

He also actively works to promote science in the public and [[physics outreach]]. As part of this effort, he regularly appears on the [[History (U.S. TV channel)|History Channel]] series [[The Universe (TV series)|''The Universe'']] and acts as a science consultant for the [[Discovery Channel]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-dec-07-ca-physics7-story.html|website=Los Angeles Times|date=7 December 2008|first=Mary|last=McNamara|title=A scientific discovery|access-date=16 December 2020| url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091005034839/http://articles.latimes.com:80/2008/dec/07/entertainment/ca-physics7 |archive-date=5 October 2009 }}</ref> Johnson founded the African Summer Theory Institute, "which brings teachers, researchers, and students of all levels together for a month-long conference on a science topic—a different one every year—to discuss, to network, and, of course, to learn."<ref>[http://www.myhero.com/myhero/hero.asp?hero=clifford_johnson_06 Science Hero: Clifford V. Johnson] ''Science Heroes''</ref> Johnson is also the author of an introductory scientific graphic novel, ''The Dialogues: Conversations about the Nature of the Universe'' . The book is a discussion on how to talk about scientific topics and exchange scientific ideas.<ref name="inverse.com"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/books/the-dialogues-conversations-about-the-nature-of-the-universe-1.4447289|title=The Dialogues: Conversations about the Nature of the Universe}}</ref>

He has also served as a science consultant for [[science fiction]] films and television shows including ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'' and ''[[Star Trek: Discovery]], and Apple TV's Dark Matter''. He made a brief [[cameo appearance]] in the 2020 film [[Palm Springs (2020 film)|''Palm Springs'']].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kohn|first=Eric|date=2020-07-09|title=Meet the Physicist Who Is Changing Movie Science, from 'Avengers' to 'Palm Springs'|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/07/movie-science-avengers-palm-springs-1234572211/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714103501/https://www.indiewire.com/2020/07/movie-science-avengers-palm-springs-1234572211/ |archive-date=14 July 2020 |access-date=2020-07-18|website=IndieWire|language=en}}</ref> In 2023, he was a guest on [[The Life Scientific]] on [[BBC Radio 4]].<ref name="Johnson_Clifford_V_2023">{{cite web|title=Making sense of black holes and movie plots|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m001hp2p|accessdate=31 January 2023}}</ref>
